title: Basie's programming and the origin of 'Fiesta in Blue'
summary: Basie's programming left Clayton few solos, until he complained and 'Fiesta in Blue' was assigned to him.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: No. Just Herschel and Lester. There was no trouble between Buddy, Don........... But sometimes Basie would get certain things in his head. Like he would just want you to play a certain way.
Yes, well I mean he was the leader.
Yes. You had to do it. But it used to kind of burn me sometimes. I would go for
four or five weeks and not play a solo on the stage unless I sneaked a solo in behind somebody that was playing a, singing a song like Helen Humes or Thelma Carpenter.

Because Basie had programmed everything in such a way, without even thinking who has got the solo, and all the solos would sometimes come out with Harry Edison playing them. So I remember, I said Basie, I says, I says, we've been playing the same concert now for five weeks at the Paramount. I says, I haven't played a thing. I says, I'm not, I might as well be back out in California somewhere.
So that's when he had 'Fiesta in Blue' made.
That wasn't made to fit you.
No, it wasn't. But I think the it might be/reason that he let me play it because Al brilliant had tried it, but he let me keep it. I mean, he made it so that I could play it. Jimmy Mundy's
Yes. Then from then on he used to play it all the time. I guess he figured I'd been complaining about not playing anything.

Harry
But everything would be heavy. And so I just finally told him, I says, I might as well be back on the Coast.
Well I don't know. I've seen that happen with other leaders and soloists and I've wondered sometimes whether it was deliberate or whether it's just really not paying any, not giving it any thought.

I think it's not giving it any thought really. Because if he had of he could have split up the numbers. That's the way Herschel was. He used to complain that Lester was playing everything. Which he was, not everything, but he was playing four-fifths of it almost. And Herschel used to complain.
